newsitem.title: LATVIA: CENTRAL BANK INSISTS LAT UNDERVALUED.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL BANK INSISTS LAT UNDERVALUED.

text.p: The Latvian central bank on Tuesday rejected comments made last week by the head of the Vereins Bank branch in Riga that the lat was over-valued and said that the Latvian currency was in fact under-valued.
The head of the new Vereins Bank branch Dietrich Schutte last week told Reuters in an interview that he thought the Latvian currency was slightly overvalued.
But the central bank in a statement said that according to purchasing power parity, the lat was undervalued.
It made a comparison of the lat to the Austrian shilling and said that although the nominal exchange rate was 0.051 the rate according to purchasing power parity was 0.022-0.023.
"Therefore we can conclude that the in no way is there an overvaluation compared to foreign currencies," the central bank said.
"On the contrary, it is two times too low," the bank added.
The central bank said that it made the comparison as Austria was considered a European average in terms of purchasing power parity.
